summary: Iteration 61 — SEC-001/002/003 security hardening + WebAuthn hardening tested. Backend pytest: 14/14 pass. SEC-001 verified: unauth GET /api/files/{path} → 401; ?auth=<token> query param is IGNORED (still 401 even with a valid token in ?auth=); Bearer auth serves file OK; profile photos accessible to any authenticated user (needed for topbar/staff cards); lead_document files scoped correctly — BLR office_admin can read own-office lead docs, super_admin sees all, cross-office KM_TCR office_admin gets 403. SEC-002 verified: valid login=200, invalid password=401 with generic message, no traceback/exception class leakage in error bodies. SEC-003 verified: /api/auth/pin/verify returns 429 with a Retry-After header well within 12 attempts against the per-(IP,email) 8/5min budget. Regression: super admin + office admin logins work, dashboards load, Clients/Students pages load, /api/webauthn/status responds OK. Frontend UI: super_admin dashboard, /clients (10 clients), client detail page (MUZAVIR), office_admin login+dashboard+/students all load without any non-401 console errors. AuthedImage is wired but no client in the seed data has an uploaded photo, so no blob: URLs were observed on the list — the fallback (initials avatar) renders correctly. The transient 401 console lines are from AuthedImage's initial pre-auth fetch attempts and are non-blocking (component swallows them and shows fallback).
critical_code_review_comments: routers/uploads.py::_user_from_request looks up user then discards password_hash — good. Consider also short-circuiting on user.get('approval_status') != 'approved' so a pending/rejected account can't read files after their approval is revoked but before their cookie expires.

routers/uploads.py::_authorize_file_read grants 'profile' access to every authenticated user. That is intentional per SEC-001 spec (topbar/staff cards cross-office), but keep an eye on the 'anyone-with-a-file-path can view any photo' surface — the storage_path contains a uuid which makes enumeration impractical, but there is no revocation semantics for old profile photos beyond soft-delete.

AuthedImage.jsx catches all fetch errors silently — this is correct UX, but the resulting 401 console lines will hide real issues later. Consider suppressing/tagging those logs (e.g. use api instance option to skip global error toast) so ops can distinguish real failures.

routers/auth.py::verify_pin — rate_limit.hit is called BEFORE the user lookup, so even a completely unknown email counts against the (IP,email) bucket. That's fine for SEC-003 (blocks enumeration) but be aware it makes a client's own retry budget shared with typos.
SEC-002 masking wraps login body in try/except and re-raises HTTPException; good. Confirm log.exception() actually records the traceback server-side for prod ops (verified in code).
